headline: EQUINOX-ORLA $18.5B MERGER GETS BC COURT STAMP TODAY — Canada's 2nd Gold Giant Closing July 31
snippet: Orla Mining sought a final order from the Supreme Court of British Columbia on July 28 to approve its business combination with Equinox Gold, with closing targeted for July 31, 2026 — creating Canada's second-largest gold producer at a combined value of approximately US$18.5 billion. Both shareholder meetings passed overwhelmingly on July 22; the court hearing is the last procedural hurdle. The combined entity will hold producing mines in Mexico, Brazil, and Nevada, giving it the scale and free cash flow to pursue additional acquisitions in a consolidating gold sector.

headline: BANYAN GOLD STRIKES VISIBLE AU AT TWO NEW YUKON ZONES — 17.80 g/t Au in First Nitra Drill 25km From AurMac (TSXV: BYN)
snippet: Banyan Gold Corp. (TSXV: BYN) announced July 28 that its first-ever drill holes at the Nitra Gold Project in Yukon — 25 kilometres west of the 100%-owned AurMac Deposit on royalty-free ground — intersected high-grade gold at two separate zones. Drillhole NT-26-001 at the newly identified Roaring Fork Zone returned 5.0 metres at 1.62 g/t gold including 0.4 metres at 17.80 g/t gold, with visible gold and bismuth-sulphosalts characteristic of the AurMac deposit mineralogy; the Seattle Creek Zone 5 km north hosts large extensional quartz veins with multiple visible gold occurrences. Both zones share structural and mineralogical hallmarks with AurMac, raising the possibility that Banyan has a district-scale system.

headline: SOUTHERN CROSS LINKS 481m CORRIDOR WITH 0.8m @ 141 g/t Au — Christina Joins Golden Dyke in 200,000m Campaign (ASX/TSX: SXGC)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Southern Cross Gold
snippet: Southern Cross Gold Consolidated (ASX: SX2 / TSX: SXGC) released July 28 drill results from the Sunday Creek Gold-Antimony Project in Victoria, Australia — the westernmost hole drilled to date intersected 481 metres of mineralisation linking the Christina prospect directly to the Golden Dyke zone, including 0.8 metres at 141.0 g/t gold. With 11 rigs running in a 200,000-metre program through Q1 2027 and 68 holes still awaiting results, the system continues to grow laterally and at depth. Chinese export restrictions on antimony — a critical mineral confirmed dominant in the upper Golden Dyke zone at up to 7.1% Sb — add a strategic layer to what is already a high-grade gold discovery.

headline: GOLD SKIDS TO $4,030 AS FOMC HIKE ODDS HIT 35% — Dollar Near 4-Week High Ahead of Warsh Decision Wednesday
snippet: Gold fell roughly 1% to around $4,030 per ounce on July 28 as a stronger U.S. dollar — hovering near a four-week high — and mounting uncertainty ahead of the FOMC decision weighed on the precious metals complex. Markets are now pricing a 35% chance of a 25-basis-point hike from Chair Warsh's committee, up sharply from 26% a week earlier, an unusually wide range of outcomes this close to a Fed meeting. Silver also declined to approximately $57.53 per ounce; the FOMC statement is due at 2:00 p.m. ET Wednesday, with the press conference at 2:30 p.m. ET — gold's direction for the next 60 days likely hinges on how the committee frames the rate path.

headline: PACIFICA SILVER FINDS NEW HIGH-GRADE SHOOT AT CLAUDIA MEXICO — 4.90m @ 428 g/t AgEq at Aguilarena (CSE: PSIL)
snippet: Pacifica Silver Corp. (CSE: PSIL) announced July 28 the identification of a new high-grade mineralised shoot north of the historical Aguilareña shaft at the Claudia Silver-Gold Project in Durango, Mexico — returning the highest gold and silver grades over the widest intervals drilled on the property. Standout intercepts from 14 additional Phase II holes include 4.90 metres at 1.21 g/t Au and 323 g/t Ag (428 g/t AgEq) and 3.05 metres at 3.91 g/t Au and 79 g/t Ag (415 g/t AgEq). A newly identified Judy anomaly is also under drill testing, with three holes reaching 402 metres vertical depth into encouraging polymetallic breccia — Phase II totals 20,000 metres.

headline: GLOBAL BATTERY MATERIALS BUYS LOMIKO AT 71% PREMIUM — Quebec Flake Graphite Consolidation Accelerates (TSXV: LMR)
snippet: Lomiko Metals Inc. (TSXV: LMR) entered into an arrangement agreement on July 28 to be acquired by Global Battery Materials Corp. for C$0.13 per share in cash — a 71% premium to the 20-day VWAP. The transaction pairs Lomiko's La Loutre natural flake graphite project in Quebec with GBM's pilot-proven anode processing technology (validated in South Korea) and its Mont-Laurier, Quebec purified graphite concentrate facility, creating a vertically integrated North American battery materials platform. With China controlling approximately 70% of global refined graphite production, Western supply chain consolidation of this type has become a strategic priority for downstream EV and energy storage manufacturers.

headline: NOBLE PLAINS URANIUM DRILLS SHIRLEY BASIN — 341 Historical Intercepts Targeted Adjacent to Ur-Energy ISR (TSXV: NOBL)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Noble Plains Uranium
snippet: Noble Plains Uranium Corp. (TSXV: NOBL) mobilized a drill rig to the Shirley Central Project in Wyoming's Shirley Basin on July 28, commencing a confirmation program designed to convert 341 historical uranium intercepts — drawn from 1,211 gamma-ray logs from exploration conducted between the 1950s and 1970s — into a compliant NI 43-101 mineral resource estimate. The 30-claim, 665-acre property sits directly adjacent to Ur-Energy's Shirley Basin in-situ recovery project, which was under construction with production planned for 2026, placing Noble Plains beside a proven, actively developing uranium operation at approximately $86/lb spot uranium.

headline: AUMEGA METALS BREAKS FIRST DRILL AT CAPE RAY WEST — Two Virgin Targets Get 10,000m Test on NL Gold Shear Zone (TSXV: AUM)
snippet: AuMEGA Metals Ltd. (TSXV: AUM / ASX: AAM) announced July 28 the commencement of diamond drilling at the Isle aux Morts Granite and Cape Ray West in Newfoundland and Labrador — two priority targets along the Cape Ray Shear Zone that have never previously been drilled. The program totals up to 10,000 metres across the two areas, with a further 5,000-metre program at Bunker Hill to follow. Both targets carry geochemical and structural signatures consistent with gold mineralisation elsewhere on the Cape Ray Shear Zone, and this maiden drill campaign provides the first real test of AuMEGA's highest-ranked untested discovery targets.

headline: SAGA METALS 57-FOR-57 AT RADAR — 19.6m @ 53.72% Fe₂O₃, 8.24% TiO₂ Advances Labrador Critical Mineral MRE (TSXV: SAGA)
snippet: SAGA Metals Corp. (TSXV: SAGA) released assays July 28 from drill holes R-0055 through R-0057 at the Radar Critical Minerals Project near Cartwright, Labrador — extending a remarkable drilling campaign where all 57 holes completed to date have intersected titanium-vanadium-iron oxide mineralisation. The standout interval in R-0057 is 19.6 metres at 53.72% Fe₂O₃, 8.24% TiO₂ and 0.377% V₂O₅, adding to a programme that has returned oxide intercepts up to 224.1 metres true width. A maiden NI 43-101 resource estimate for the Trapper Zone is targeted for late 2026; both titanium and vanadium appear on Canadian and U.S. critical minerals lists.

headline: GOLDSEEK: GOLD HUNTING FOR A FLOOR AFTER $4,030 SLAM — Fits-and-Starts Pattern Points to Accumulation, Not Breakdown
snippet: A GoldSeek analysis examines gold's pattern of fitful selloffs punctuated by recovery attempts in the $4,000–4,100 range, arguing this is consistent with a market rotating from short-term traders into longer-term accumulators rather than a clean breakdown. The piece notes that structural demand drivers — central bank buying, geopolitical hedging flows, and dollar weakening trends — remain intact, and that the current weakness reflects FOMC tactical uncertainty rather than a change in the fundamental case. How gold handles the $4,000–4,030 zone in the immediate aftermath of Wednesday's rate decision is identified as the critical technical tell for the next two months.
